quote: Die Ausartungen und möglichen Typen der allgemeinen linearen Transformation von $n$ Variabeln
english: The degenerations and possible types of the general linear transformation of n variables.
topic: A list of research problems and notes on invariant theory: gap-free assembly of bodies in several dimensions, types of linear transformations, skew invariants of binary forms of odd degree, complete systems of forms, and canonical forms.

triage.modern_statement: Classify the general linear transformation x -> Ax of n variables (a projective collineation of P^{n-1}) up to change of coordinates (conjugation A -> PAP^{-1}): list every possible 'type' (normal form) and describe how the generic type (n distinct eigenvalues, diagonalisable) degenerates into the special types when eigenvalues coincide or the matrix stops being diagonalisable. In modern terms this is the Jordan normal form / Weierstrass elementary divisors, with types labelled by Segre characteristics, plus the order in which conjugacy classes (orbits) lie in each other's closures.
triage.answered_by: The classification of types was mostly done before Hilbert wrote the note. Weierstrass did it with elementary divisors (1858 preliminary memoir, 1868 paper). Camille Jordan gave the canonical form in his Traité des substitutions (1870). Hamburger linked the two results in 1872, and Corrado Segre's 1884 characteristic notation is used to label the types. The 'degeneration' part, read as which orbits lie in the closure of others, was settled for nilpotent matrices by Gerstenhaber (1959) and Hesselink (1976); the closure order is the dominance order on partitions.

evidence.claim: The Jordan normal form theorem comes from Weierstrass in 1868 and Camille Jordan in 1870, and is called one of the seminal results of linear algebra.
Weierstrass proved his elementary-divisor results in a preliminary 1858 memoir and in 1868.
Hamburger pointed out in 1872 how Jordan's canonical form connects to Weierstrass' elementary divisors theorem.
Jordan's Traité (1870) contains the Jordan normal form theorem (over a finite field), apparently without knowledge of Weierstrass' earlier results.
Corrado Segre proposed the Segre classification in 1884.

Conjugacy classes of nilpotent n×n matrices correspond one-to-one to partitions of n. By the Gerstenhaber–Hesselink theorem, their orbit closures are described by the natural (dominance) order on partitions.
The original source for the dominance/closure result on nilpotent classes appears to be Gerstenhaber (1959).

triage.why: The wording 'types of the general linear transformation of n variables' fits the classical classification of collineations by elementary divisors / Segre characteristic, which Weierstrass and Jordan had already solved. Hilbert most likely wrote it down as a study or exposition topic in an invariant-theoretic setting, not as a new unsolved problem. It is not among his 23 published problems or the 24th problem. Reading 'Ausartungen' as orbit-closure degenerations is my modern interpretation, and on that reading Gerstenhaber and Hesselink settled the nilpotent case. Orbit-closure geometry in general is still studied, but this specific question for GL_n is closed. Confidence is medium because the note is short and I cannot check Hilbert's exact intent.
